2. By means of the present writ petitions,
petitioners have sought quashing of the F.I.R./
Case Crime No.0063 of 2025, under Section 120-
B, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 506 I.P.C. and Section
3(1)(r) and Section 3(1)(s) of the Scheduled Castes
and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989, registered at Police Station Buggawala,
District Haridwar. It is reported that, during the
course of investigation, Section 3(1)(r) and
Section 3(1)(s) of the Scheduled Castes and
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989 were dropped, as petitioners belong too
belong to the Scheduled Caste Community.
3. An F.I.R. was lodged by respondent no.3
inter alia stating that someone impersonated and
executed sale deed in favour of Kunwar Pal, who
is paralyzed and is bedridden.
4. Mange Ram (Petitioner in WPCRL No.1719
of 2025) and Amit Kumar (Petitioner no.2 in
WPCRL No.1643 of 2025) was witness of the said
sale deed, while sale deed was executed in favour
of Pooran Singh (Petitioner no.1 in WPCRL
No.1643 of 2025). Now, joint compounding

applications have been filed on behalf of the
petitioners and respondent no.3, duly supported
by their respective affidavits. It is further stated
that, during the pendency of the present
proceedings, the parties have amicably resolved
their dispute and have arrived at a settlement
amongst themselves. Respondent no.3 has
categorically stated that he does not wish to
pursue the matter any further and has no
objection if the proceedings arising out of the
impugned F.I.R. are brought to an end in
accordance with law.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits
that, during the pendency of the present
proceedings, the parties have amicably settled
their dispute and have entered into a compromise
voluntarily and without any coercion or undue
influence. He, therefore, submits that, in view of
the settlement arrived at between the parties and
the stand taken by respondent no.3, the
proceedings arising out of the impugned F.I.R.
may be permitted to be compounded in
accordance with law.
6. Learned counsel for respondent no.3
submits that dispute has now been amicably
settled between the parties, therefore, his client
wants to close the matter to ensure that peace is
restored.
7. Today, petitioners and respondent no.3 are
present in Court today, who are duly identified by
their respective counsels.
8. Both the parties also made a statement
that, in view of the settlement, they want to close
the matter.
9. Learned State Counsel vehemently opposed
the compounding application.
10. Having regard to the nature of offence and
also considering the broad guidelines issued by
Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs
State of Punjab reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303
and Narinder Singh & others Vs State of Punjab
& another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466, request
of the petitioner deserves to be acceded to.
11. Since the parties have entered into a
compromise, therefore, possibility of the trial

UKHC010202952025
2026:UHC:9052
resulting into conviction of the accused is remote
and bleak and, that being so, continuation of
criminal proceedings would visit the accused with
great oppression, prejudice and injustice. Rather,
it would tantamount to abuse of process of law.
Ends of justice would be met if criminal
proceedings are put to an end, because this
would allow the parties to translate their decision
to live in peace in the reality. The only
consideration for the compromise reached
between the parties seems to be their desire to
burry the hatchet for all times to come.
Resolution of a dispute by way of a compromise
between two warring groups, therefore, should
attract the immediate and prompt attention of a
Court which should endeavour to give full effect
to the same unless such compromise is abhorrent
to lawful composition of the society or would
promote savagery.
12. In view of above discussion, the writ
petitions are allowed. F.I.R./ Case Crime No.0063
of 2025, under Section 120-B, 420, 467, 468, 471
and 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)(r) and Section
3(1)(s) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled
Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989,
registered at Police Station Buggawala, District
Haridwar is hereby quashed along with all the
proceedings emanating therefrom, qua the
petitioners.
13. Compounding applications are,
accordingly, disposed of.
